title: Explicit canonical Mayer--Vietoris triangle and direct-image comparison data
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme with derived module categories on $X$ and its opens. For a two-open cover $X=U\cup V$ and $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$, define $I(E)$ by the fixed functorial K-injective resolution of a localization preimage, and $e_E:Q(I(E))\cong E$ by the inverse localized resolution map. Derive the fixed module restriction adjunctions $a_T$. Define $\delta_E$ by transporting the boundary of the concrete Mayer--Vietoris short exact sequence of $I(E)$ along $e_E$ and the explicit intersection comparison. Define $\operatorname{MV}(E)$ with first arrow the pair of units of $a_U,a_V$, second arrow the difference of their nested restriction maps, and third arrow $\delta_E$. For $h:X\to Y$ and an open $T\subseteq Y$, define $c_T:Rh_*Rj_{h^{-1}T,*}(E|_{h^{-1}T})\cong Rj_{T,*}((Rh_*E)|_T)$ using composition isomorphisms normalized by their right-derived unit equation and the derived sectionwise open-restriction identity. Define the middle comparison as the biproduct comparison followed by $c_U\oplus c_V$. All objects and maps are explicitly constructed; no boundary or comparison is selected from a bare existence assertion. Derived restriction is an abbreviation of the existing exact derived functor, elaborating its exactness witnesses once for reuse.

proof.text: Choose the fixed functorial K-injective resolution of the localization preimage of E, and invert its localized resolution map. Derive the fixed module restriction adjunction. Transport the concrete short-exact-sequence boundary using the explicit intersection comparison and this resolution isomorphism. All these are real constructions. The resolution is a named construction with proved K-injectivity and injective-term instances, so consumers need not unfold the resolution functor merely to reuse these properties.

Select the composition isomorphism by the determining right-derived unit equation of exists_derivedModuleDirectImageComposition. Construct the open-restriction comparison by deriving the sectionwise identity: use rightDerivedFunctorCompMapDerivedCategoryIso, rightDerivedFunctorNatIso and rightDerivedFunctorCompIso, followed by rightDerivedFunctorIsoMapDerivedCategory. Compose these comparisons and the additive biproduct comparison. No isomorphism is selected from mere Nonempty. The construction uses the generic right-derived functor composition and exact-functor comparison declarations from WeilConjectures.CategoryTheory.DerivedCategory.RightDerivedFunctor.MapDerivedCategory and Comp directly; the bare Nonempty wrapper of the scheme restriction theorem is not used. The image triangle is a named definition of mapTriangle.obj, with shift commutation elaborated once; its distinguishedness is proved using the triangulated direct-image instance.
